sample.name: Fraenkel Gallery
facts: Founded by Jeffrey Fraenkel on September 11, 1979.
Its first exhibition showed 19th-century California photographs by Carleton Watkins.
Address: 49 Geary Street, San Francisco

sample.name: Hosfelt Gallery
facts: Founded in 1996 by Todd Hosfelt.
Moved to an 8,900-square-foot space on Utah Street in 2012.
Address: 260 Utah Street, San Francisco

sample.name: Precita Eyes Mural Arts and Visitors Center
facts: Precita Eyes Muralists Association was founded in 1977 by Susan and Luis Cervantes.
Bought the 24th Street building in 1998, near Balmy Alley.
The first organization added to the Legacy Business Registry, in 2015.

sample.name: Crown Point Press
facts: Founded in 1962 by Kathan Brown.
Publishes etchings and shows the prints in a gallery beside its studios and bookstore.
Address: 20 Hawthorne Street, San Francisco

sample.name: Chinese Historical Society of America
facts: Housed in the Julia Morgan designed Chinatown YWCA building completed in 1932.
The society was established in 1962.
Wheelchair accessible

sample.name: Wood Line
facts: Andy Goldsworthy's 1,200-foot sculpture of eucalyptus branches, completed in 2011.
Built from branches cleared in the Presidio's forest rejuvenation program.
Intended to fade back into the earth over time.

sample.name: Museum of the African Diaspora
facts: Occupies the first three floors of the St. Regis Museum Tower.
Has no permanent collection and presents rotating exhibitions by artists of the African diaspora.
A Smithsonian Affiliate.

sample.name: Museum of Craft and Design
facts: Founded in 2004 as the San Francisco Museum of Craft+Design.
Moved to the American Industrial Center in Dogpatch in April 2013.
Its building was originally the American Can Company plant from 1915.

sample.name: SFJAZZ Center
facts: Opened in January 2013 at Fell and Franklin streets.
Described as the first stand-alone structure in the country built specifically for jazz.
Designed by architect Mark Cavagnero, with a 700-seat auditorium and a 100-seat lab.

sample.name: Walt Disney Family Museum
facts: Opened to the public in October 2009.
The Disney family, led by Diane Disney Miller, funded the reuse of three historic Presidio buildings.
Is the first museum dedicated to the life and work of Walt Disney.

sample.name: Letterform Archive
facts: Founded in 2014 by graphic designer Rob Saunders from his private collection.
Opened to visitors in February 2015.
Collects materials on the history of lettering, typography, printing and graphic design.

sample.name: San Francisco Railway Museum
facts: Market Street Railway opened it in 2006 across from the Ferry Building.
Exhibits cover F-line streetcars, cable cars and the 1906 earthquake; admission is free.
Founded in 2006

sample.name: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
facts: Established in 1993 as part of the Yerba Buena Gardens redevelopment.
The Galleries and Forum were designed by architect Fumihiko Maki.
Includes the 757-seat Blue Shield of California Theater.

sample.name: American Bookbinders Museum
facts: Opened as a private museum in 2009.
Relocated in 2015 to a larger space in South of Market, opening to the public.
Covers the history and tools of bookbinding from the colonial era to the early 20th century.

sample.name: African American Art & Culture Complex
facts: Formed in 1989 when the Wajumbe Cultural Institution and the SF African American Historical Society joined forces.
Includes art galleries, performance spaces, dance studios and a library and archives.
Address: 762 Fulton St, San Francisco

sample.name: GLBT History Museum
facts: The society was founded in 1985.
The museum opened in January 2011 as the first stand-alone LGBTQ history museum in the US.
Founded in 1985

sample.name: Haas-Lilienthal House
facts: Queen Anne house designed by Peter R. Schmidt and built in 1886 for William Haas.
The Haas-Lilienthal family lived here until 1973, when the house went to SF Heritage.
San Francisco Landmark #69 and listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
